root_cause.text: The `ext4_mb_release()` function only flushes pending discard work when the `DISCARD` mount option is currently set, failing to drain queued work that was populated when the filesystem was previously mounted with the discard option before being remounted with `nodiscard`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes the conditional check `if (test_opt(sb, DISCARD))` that guarded the `flush_work(&sbi->s_discard_work)` call. The vulnerability occurs because when a filesystem is remounted from `-o discard` to `-o nodiscard`, the `EXT4_MOUNT_DISCARD` flag is cleared, but any pending `s_discard_work` queued during the discard-enabled phase remains unprocessed. The original code would skip flushing this work during unmount if the current mount state has `nodiscard` set, leaving orphaned work items in the queue.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove DISCARD option guard from discard work flush to ensure proper cleanup of discard operations during module release regardless of mount options.
intent_record.what: Removed the `if (test_opt(sb, DISCARD))` conditional guard wrapping the discard work flush and list check, moving the `flush_work()` and `WARN_ON_ONCE()` calls outside the conditional block to execute unconditionally.
intent_record.how: Previously, the discard work flush and warning check only executed when the DISCARD mount option was enabled. Now these operations execute regardless of the DISCARD option setting. This ensures the discard work is always drained and the discard list is always checked for emptiness during ext4_mb_release(), even when DISCARD is not explicitly enabled.

bic_trace_step.reason: The commit introduces the vulnerable construct in `ext4_mb_release()` at lines 3476-3483. The function only flushes pending discard work when `test_opt(sb, DISCARD)` is true: `if (test_opt(sb, DISCARD)) { flush_work(&sbi->s_discard_work); ... }`. This is the exact vulnerability described in the root cause: the function fails to drain queued work that was populated when the filesystem was previously mounted with the discard option before being remounted with `nodiscard`. If a filesystem is remounted from `discard` to `nodiscard`, the condition `test_opt(sb, DISCARD)` will be false, causing the function to skip the `flush_work()` call entirely, leaving pending discard work items in `sbi->s_discard_list` undrained. The fix would require unconditionally flushing the work or checking if the list is non-empty regardless of the current mount option setting.
